about: Santa's troublemaking older brother has to help out at the North Pole in the busy week before Christmas.

    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersRepo man Chicago-style hot dogsBeef frank in a poppy seed bun with mustard, relish, tomato, pickle, peppersHow to make it8 beef frankfurts8 hot dog buns1 tbsp poppy seeds1 bottle American mustard1 jar sweet green relish1 white onion, diced2 tomatoes, cut into wedges8 dill pickle spears16 pickled peppers1 tsp celery saltSimmer the frankfurts in water, then grill briefly for colour.Steam or warm the buns and sprinkle the tops with poppy seeds.Put a frankfurt in each bun, add mustard and relish, then onion, tomato, a pickle spear and pickled peppers.Finish with a pinch of celery salt.Iced gingerbread menSpiced ginger cookies cut into men and piped with icingHow to make it100g butter100g golden syrup80g brown sugar300g self-raising flour2 tsp ground ginger150g icing sugarMelt the butter with the golden syrup and brown sugar, then mix in the flour and ginger to a dough.Roll out and cut gingerbread men.Bake at 180°C.Cool completely.Mix the icing sugar with a little water and pipe on faces and buttons.MainsClaus family honey mustard glazed hamHoney Dijon clove ham, the dinner Nick talked him intoHow to make it2.5kg half leg ham1 tbsp cloves120ml honey3 tbsp Dijon mustard60g brown sugar1 orange, juiced1kg potatoes, halved3 tbsp vegetable oil150g green beans1 bunch broccolini30g butterRemove the rind from the ham, score the fat in a diamond pattern and stud with cloves.Simmer the honey, mustard, sugar and orange juice for the glaze.Bake the ham at 180°C, brushing with glaze every so often. Roast the potatoes in oil alongside.Toss the beans and broccolini in butter.Slice the ham thickly to serve.Siblings Anonymous chicken pot pieFred's support group for famous people's brothersHow to make it800g chicken thigh fillets2 leeks2 carrots40g butter3 tbsp plain flour400ml chicken stock150ml thickened cream150g frozen peas1 thyme2 sheets of puff pastry1 eggBrown the diced chicken in half the butter, then add the sliced leeks, diced carrots and the rest of the butter and cook for 6 minutes.Stir in the flour, then the stock, cream and thyme leaves and simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas.Heat the oven to 200°C. Spoon the filling into a pie dish and cover with the pastry, pressing the edges.Brush with beaten egg, cut a steam hole and bake for 30 minutes until puffed and golden.SweetsMother Claus's choc chip cookiesBrown butter milk chocolate chip cookies with sea salt, served with milkHow to make it125g butter150g brown sugar50g caster sugar1 egg1 tsp vanilla extract220g plain flour1/2 tsp bicarbonate of soda150g milk chocolate, chopped1 tsp sea salt flakes1 L cold full cream milk, to serveMelt the butter and cook until golden brown and nutty, then cool.Beat in both sugars, the egg and vanilla. Stir in the flour, bicarbonate of soda and chocolate.Roll into balls and chill.Bake at 180°C until golden at the edges.Sprinkle with sea salt and serve warm with cold milk.DrinksEverybody's nice marshmallow cocoaToasted marshmallow hot chocolate, for kids Fred marked niceHow to make it1 L full cream milk150g milk chocolate, chopped1 tbsp cocoa powder16 large marshmallows1/2 tsp ground cinnamonHeat the milk until steaming, then whisk in the chocolate and cocoa until smooth and frothy.Pour into heatproof mugs, pile marshmallows on top and put the mugs on a tray under a hot grill, watching closely, until puffed and golden.Dust with cinnamon and serve.
